At least that was the story in the movie. Sorry i know its off-topic. Will not do that again for a while. 4th 😛 Curious, do you all have plans to offer staking services post-merge? We may merge with a certain large pool or open our own we will see Tried to scoop up all the eth devs from sparkpool 😛 Canadian laws don’t make it easy to open a staking pool 😑 🇨🇦 ~~Does anyone have an example of a contract live today that requires 1.8MB of calldata?~~ Looks like I'm the 10th person to ask for this. 😬 I wouldn't say it's FUD because there *have* been instances of using >1 MB per block so it's not like there 0 demand for it Very few, and none that would appear to have transactions that couldn't be broken across multiple blocks. (BTW, I think that there are even fewer than Nick suggested, as I believe his query should be -300 rather than +299). that's fair I didn't look too deeply at it Hi. I have a dumb question about PBS. Do the builders get the gas fees for the blocks they win? I've been thinking they do, but I can't see any explicit references to this in the proposals yes Good- thanks. I really like your parallel PBS idea. Just working on a response to it 👍 👍 Look forward to reading! Ace. Fancy me writing a MEV auction proposal. Never say never eh Since it’s likely a few eth 2.0 pools will rugpull or get hacked is there a chance there will be a dao style fork or is that impossible now? In the early days it’s entirely foreseeable to see a 10-20% loss rate among validators It would be good to have an insurance fund validator pools could pay into 😅 it's ~~impossible~~ very very unlikely, verging on impossible. it opens a can of worms for which necessitates a system of review and correction for any lost/ stolen funds which would become incredibly complex also diminishes the non-interventionist stance that has been nurtured in the years following the DAO hack we've already seen unfortunate losses from staking services Not like I'm the one making decisions or anything, but I would say that while the beaconchain is still in its isolated environment, hard forks to restore bugs on it is an option. That's because it doesn't mess with the economic activity on the EL. Not sure about rugpulls though. After the merge, I'd say it's almost certain nothing would happen in such a scenario (judging by e.g. EIP-999). Adding to that, I would say that quite a few parties offering custodial staking services have already done so for many years for other coins, and/or are an exchange having access to much more funds than just what is staked on Ethereum (say Kraken, Binance and Coinbase). If they were to rugpull, I'd say they would have done so already. (not advocating the use of custodial staking services by the way; solo staking is the way to go 😉 ) the low probability of irregular state changes shouldn't preclude flexpool or other operators from considering a collective insurance fund, it's an interesting idea though it would be hard to verify some situations eg. "i've lost these private keys" - you can't prove a negative like that. there's also the governance overhead of managing claims which makes me think we won't see anything like this soon The network is not here for validators, the validators are here for the network (and are paid for their services). Validators losing money because they don't do their job properly is exactly how PoS is supposed to work. If we bail them out we unermine the security of the chain. So no, I would never expect a bail out for validators. 32 made sense back when eth was $400 but now that it’s 10x it’s hard to offer secure non custodial staking. It’s impossible for any setup that cares about security to offer custodial staking on validation when its really new and still immature/not compete And I completely expect some major staking pools to fail. Mt gox was a great example and they it was a lot less complicated to secure it. Collective insurance does seem attractive but also it’s hard to ensure given that 100% is like 10-20 years of staking fees Not going to argue that 32 ETH is a lot now. I agree that we need more things like Rocket Pool, SSV, and changes to the protocol to bring the barrier to entry down where possible. I also expect some services to fail in some ways or another (some already have lost _some_ funds due to slashable offenses as Trent said). I personally would say that's the price you pay / risk you take when using custodial services. If you can provide an insured option at a premium, that's great for those interested in such a thing. when i run docker logs lighthouse_beacon -f --tail=20 i get this error: Failed to parse enr-address: <myip> running vscode on mac Why is that? political environment is pretty different now and sets a bad precedent i modified my response to include more nuance That doesn't make it impossible. And probably a discussion about bad precedent is off topic for off topic. I don't think rug pulls is something we should be preparing for. But certainly believe we should have already some mechanism in place to account for a mayor fuck up and go back a finalized chain. excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content:
Not like I'm the one making decisions or anything, but I would say that while the beaconchain is still in its isolated environment, hard forks to restore bugs on it is an option. That's because it doesn't mess with the economic activity on the EL. Not sure about rugpulls though.
After the merge, I'd say it's almost certain nothing would happen in such a scenario (judging by e.g. EIP-999).

Adding to that, I would say that quite a few parties offering custodial staking services have already done so for many years for other coins, and/or are an exchange having access to much more funds than just what is staked on Ethereum (say Kraken, Binance and Coinbase). If they were to rugpull, I'd say they would have done so already.

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: (not advocating the use of custodial staking services by the way; solo staking is the way to go 😉 )

excerpts.author: trent_vanepps
excerpts.content:
the low probability of irregular state changes shouldn't preclude flexpool or other operators from considering a collective insurance fund, it's an interesting idea

though it would be hard to verify some situations eg. "i've lost these private keys" - you can't prove a negative like that. there's also the governance overhead of managing claims which makes me think we won't see anything like this soon

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: The network is not here for validators, the validators are here for the network (and are paid for their services).  Validators losing money because they don't do their job properly is exactly how PoS is supposed to work. If we bail them out we unermine the security of the chain. So no, I would never expect a bail out for validators.

Not going to argue that 32 ETH is a lot now. I agree that we need more things like Rocket Pool, SSV, and changes to the protocol to bring the barrier to entry down where possible.
I also expect some services to fail in some ways or another (some already have lost _some_ funds due to slashable offenses as Trent said). I personally would say that's the price you pay / risk you take when using custodial services. If you can provide an insured option at a premium, that's great for those interested in such a thing.
